quickAnswer.question: How do I get a transcript of an Instagram video?
quickAnswer.answer: Copy the link to a public Instagram Reel or video and paste it into TranscriptX. It reads the audio and generates the transcript within seconds, across more than 100 languages, ready to read, copy, edit or download. You never sign up, and there is nothing to download onto your device.

content: An Instagram transcript is the spoken content of a Reel or video written out as text. Whatever the creator says on camera — the hook, the steps, the story — becomes words you can read, search and copy instead of tapping through the clip again to catch a line you missed.

Short video is why this is so handy on Instagram. A Reel is built to be watched once and swiped past, and the useful part is often a single sentence: the tip in a 15-second tutorial, the claim in a product review, the line that made the Reel go viral. An Instagram video transcript pins that line down as text before it disappears from your feed.

This page exists to do one job well — get the words out of an Instagram video. Whether you think of it as getting the transcript, generating one with AI, or converting the Reel to text, the outcome is identical, so it all lives on one tool instead of being spread across near-duplicate pages.
TranscriptX produces the transcript free, right in the browser, with no sign-up at any point.

sections.h2: How to Get a Transcript From an Instagram Video or Reel

steps.content: Open the Reel or video, tap the three-dot menu and choose Copy Link, or copy the URL from the address bar on desktop. The post needs to be public.
Drop the link into the box above. Getting an Instagram transcript from a link takes no upload and no account — the tool reads the video straight from the URL.
TranscriptX listens to the audio, detects the language on its own across 100+ languages, separates each speaker, and writes the words out with punctuation.
Read it, copy the whole thing or a single line, edit it, translate it, or download it to keep.

sections.h2: An Instagram Transcript Generator That Works Without Captions
content: Most Reels have no clean caption track to lift, and the auto-captions that appear on screen are often wrong or missing punctuation. So TranscriptX works as an Instagram transcript generator: it builds the text from the audio itself rather than depending on captions the creator may never have added.

That means you can transcribe Instagram video audio even when there is nothing on screen to copy. The generator handles fast talking, trending audio and background music, and it labels separate speakers when a Reel has a duet, a collab or an interview clip. Instagram video transcription runs the same way in every language it hears, so a Reel in Portuguese or Arabic comes back as text in that language, detected automatically.
Because it works from the audio, the result is usually cleaner than Instagram's own captions, especially on accents and fast, casual speech.

If you do not think in terms of the word transcript and just want to turn an Instagram video to text, this is the same tool under a name that fits. Paste the link and the spoken content comes back as plain, readable text.

It reads the sound of the clip, so Instagram audio to text works whether the point of the video is a person talking to camera, a voiceover on a tutorial, or narration over B-roll. Creators lift a viral Reel's script to study why it landed, marketers pull talking points out of a competitor's video, and language learners read a fast native-speaker Reel slowly once it is text on the page.

sections.h2: What You Can Transcribe on Instagram
intro: If there is speech in it, TranscriptX can turn it into text. The formats people convert most, and why the transcript helps for each:

items.content: Short and fast, with the value usually in one line. A transcript captures the hook or the tip as text before the Reel scrolls out of the feed, so you can save it, study it or write your own version.
A talking-head update or an explainer posted to a feed becomes quotable, searchable text rather than a clip you replay to reference a point.
Longer-form Instagram video — interviews, tutorials, sit-down talks — turns into a document you can skim for the part that matters instead of scrubbing the timeline.
An Instagram Live that was saved and posted becomes readable text, with each speaker labelled, so a Q&A or a co-hosted session reads as a clear back-and-forth.
Recipes, workouts and tutorials packed into a short Reel become step-by-step text you can follow without pausing and rewinding every few seconds.

content: As soon as the transcript appears it is ready to work with. Take the whole thing or pull out one quote, tidy up the filler, or run it through translation into another language right where you are.

When you want it saved rather than on screen, you can download Instagram transcript text as TXT, DOCX, PDF, SRT or VTT — plain text for reading and pasting, a document for editing, a fixed file for sharing, or a timed caption file if the Reel needs subtitles.

Looking for the written caption a creator posted under the Reel rather than the spoken words? That is a different job — the [Instagram Caption Downloader](/instagram-caption-downloader) grabs the post's description instead. And across platforms, the [TikTok Transcript](/tiktok-transcript) and [YouTube Transcript](/youtube-transcript) tools do the same as this one for those sites.

How closely the transcript matches the Reel depends mostly on the audio. A creator speaking clearly to camera comes back close to word for word, while loud background music, several people talking at once, or very fast, mumbled speech will need more review.
The passages worth checking are names, numbers, brand names and hashtags read aloud — quick to fix against the video compared with transcribing the whole thing by hand.

TranscriptX recognises speech in over 100 languages and detects which one it is hearing automatically, so an Instagram video in any language comes back as a transcript in that same language, with speakers kept separate throughout.

Over 100. The spoken language is detected automatically, so the transcript comes back in whatever language the Instagram video was recorded in.
